data.narrative:
Lumotive is a Series B semiconductor chip company founded by Gleb Akselrod that has raised $72M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public comparables in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including same-stage and adjacent-stage peers such as Positron AI, SambaNova Systems, d-Matrix, and DEEPX.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using $72M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier typical of the sector, implies a valuation of $137M. Peer-median anchoring across the 4 same-sector comparables yields a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range spanning $529M (DEEPX) to $11.0B (SambaNova Systems). Public-comp anchoring using semiconductor P/S multiples (21.0x median across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) is not applicable, as Lumotive's revenue is not publicly available. 

The two applicable methods produce a triangulated range of $116M (low) to $1.7B (high), with a median of $818M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding where Lumotive sits within the peer distribution—specifically, whether it tracks closer to earlier-stage, lower-valued comparables or to growth-stage AI chip players commanding higher multiples. Stage of capital deployment, commercial traction, and IP defensibility would be key inputs to refining this range.
